Hi Dana — thanks for the clear ask. High level: we can produce both an enriched (full) audit bundle and a compact events-only export. Typical formats we support are newline-delimited JSON (JSONL) and Parquet; CSV is possible but loses nested metadata so we generally avoid it for forensic exports.

A quick summary of options (short):
- Full enriched bundle: every event + context (actor metadata, request/response headers, pre/post config snapshots). Format: JSONL or Parquet. Good for forensic work and SIG mapping.
- Compact event feed: canonical event lines (timestamp, event_type, actor, resource, outcome). Format: JSONL. Good for ingestion to SIEMs.
- Streaming export: short-lived websocket or streaming S3 transfer for incremental pulls (useful for large date ranges).
- Signed snapshot: gzipped bundle + SHA256 manifest + optional PKCS7 signature.

ETA: for a 12-month ad-hoc bundle we target 5 business days from confirmed scope and delivery method. For recurring exports we can set up a daily or monthly Parquet feed to your S3.

Couple of clarifying Qs before we proceed:
1) Do you need redaction of IP addresses, or will pseudonymization (hashed ip) suffice for your auditors?
2) Any particular mapping to CAIQ/SIG question ids you want included in the manifest? We can attach a control map csv.

I'm attaching a short evidence-options matrix that lists event classes and their export variants so you can pick the right bundle. Once you confirm scope we’ll schedule the run and provide transfer details (presigned S3 or SFTP).

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

Hi Dana — Neha from Security/Trust here. I wanted to provide the technical runbook details so you and your auditors can evaluate the output. Below is what we propose for the 12-month export and how each piece maps to typical SIG/CAIQ and SOC 2 evidence requests.

1) Event types included (recommended minimal set):
- admin.sign_in (successful/failed) — maps to SIG-IS-Auth/CAIQ-AUTH
- api_key.rotate / api_key.create / api_key.disable — maps to access key lifecycle controls
- role.grant / role.revoke — admin role changes
- deployment.create / deployment.rollback / model.publish — deployment/change history
- kms.key.use / kms.key.rotate — key management events
- console.config_change (settings, retention, CORS, webhooks)
- audit.view / audit.export (who viewed exports) — important for proof of least privilege

2) Retention & sampling:
- Primary retention: 24 months in hot store (searchable).
- Archive: 7 years in cold store (compressed Parquet + checksums) for customers that opt in.
- For very long windows we materialize Parquet partitions by month to make transfers small and resumable.

3) Redaction & pseudonymization:
- PII fields (user_email, ip_address) can be pseudonymized (sha256(email+salt)) or redacted on export depending on your auditor needs. Raw values are available to your security org when we deliver to a controlled destination and after NDA.

4) Export formats & integrity:
- JSONL (canonical logs) — human-readable, simple to consume.
- Parquet (columnar) — efficient for large windows and analytics.
- Each bundle comes with SHA256 manifest and optional PKCS7 signature (signed by Redwood key). We can provide public cert if you want to verify signature chain.

5) Transfer & encryption:
- Recommended: direct S3 push to customer bucket (we assume least privilege role; transfer uses customer-managed KMS key).
- Alternatives: pre-signed S3 link, SFTP, or encrypted HTTPS download.

6) Mapping & deliverables:
- We’ll include a control map file (CSV) that links event classes to SIG/CAIQ question ids and SOC 2 criteria.
- A short integrity report (checksums, record counts) and a sampling of raw events for auditor review are included.

7) SLA & access control:
- Ad-hoc bundle: 5 business days SLA after scope confirmed.
- Emergency expedited: 48–72 hours for an additional fee and approval.

If that looks good I’ll draft the export manifest and a minimal ACL for the S3 bucket transfer. Also attaching a short runbook of the steps we’ll follow.

Neha Kapoor
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
